## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af660b1d4ce191b815025f8ae22ecbadac375563`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card objectui#11220 (body; comments `5913805765` triage grade, `5916283812` claim, `5916966124` dev report), PR objectui#11250 (body, 3 files, net diff against `main` at merge-base `b32e7debc8`), and the head's check-runs. Diff: `.changeset/11220-screen-select-placeholder-i18n.md` (+19), `packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.selectPlaceholderLocale-11220.test.tsx` (+103), `packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.tsx` (+12/−6). Matches the dev report's `files_changed`.

Check-runs on the head: 43, all `completed`; 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (dependabot and the two conditional coverage jobs), 0 failure, 0 `in_progress`. The `check:i18n-keys` step runs inside the `Type Check` job (ci.yml step "Verify t() call-site keys exist in the en locale pack"), which is `success`; `Lint`, `Test`, all eight `Test (shard i/8)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Changeset Bump Policy` / `Changeset Declaration` / `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Pre-Install Import Graph Check`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all `success`.

- **Fallback through the i18n path, an existing key, no literal list — right.** `ScreenFieldInput` now reads `field.placeholder ?? t('common.select', { defaultValue: 'Select…' })` with `t` from `useObjectTranslation()` (`@object-ui/i18n`, already `workspace:*` in app-shell's dependencies, so no new edge; `Pre-Install Import Graph Check` green). `common.select` exists under `common` in all ten built-in packs at the head: ar `اختر…`, de `Auswählen…`, en `Select…`, es `Seleccionar…`, fr `Sélectionner…`, ja `選択…`, ko `선택…`, pt `Selecionar…`, ru `Выбрать…`, zh `选择…` (`packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts`). It is the key the object form's lookup picker already reads in the same spot (`LookupField.tsx:1387`, `t('common.select')`), and this screen's own `lookup` arm renders that widget, so choosing `common.select` over `common.selectOption` ("Select an option", `SelectField.tsx:208`) is the grade's "existing select… key" read right. No pack was edited.
- **Inline default matches en byte-for-byte — right.** Head `ScreenView.tsx:391` and `en.ts:137` both hold `Select` + U+2026 (`e2 80 a6`), so `check:i18n-keys` class 3 (`default-value-drift`) is satisfied. The gate does read the site: `PACK_HOOK` is `/^use[A-Za-z0-9_]*(Translation|Translate|T)$/`, which matches `useObjectTranslation`, and the class keys on a binding named `t`/`tt` — which is why the rename below was needed.
- **Bare hook, no provider — right.** `useObjectTranslation` (`provider.tsx:889`) returns react-i18next's not-ready `t` wrapped in `interpolateFallback` when no instance is found; not-ready `t` answers `options.defaultValue` verbatim and the raw key only without one. So a host mounting without `I18nProvider` sees `Select…`, never `common.select`. The pin's provider-less case is a real measurement, not a pass-through of a leaked global: `createI18n` does install a global via `initReactI18next`, but the repo's `vitest.setup.i18n-global.ts` (`installI18nGlobalReset`, objectui#4514) restores the pointer between tests, consistent with the dev's ablation (b) going red on that case alone.
- **Rename `t` to `kind` — right, behaviour unchanged.** Base `ScreenFieldInput` bound `const t = (field.type || 'text').toLowerCase()` and compared it at `:369`, `:397`, `:400`, `:403`; the head binds `kind` with the same initialiser and compares it at the same four sites with the same operands; no other bare `t` identifier remains in that function (the file's only other `t`, `:166`–`:167`, is a different function's local and is untouched). The translator is bound first and unconditionally, before every early return, and `ScreenFieldInput` is rendered only as a JSX element (`ScreenView.tsx:311`), so hook order holds.
- **`||` to `??`, authored `''` kept — right and pinned.** The pin case "an authored empty placeholder stays empty" asserts the trigger's trimmed text is `''` and contains neither the zh nor the en word; the changeset names this as the one deliberate behaviour change. The claim states it as "`||` becomes `??`"; the PR body and changeset spell out the kept behaviour, which is where a reader looks.
- **Both pinned surfaces reach the fix — right.** `FlowRunner` (already under `useObjectTranslation`) and Studio's `ScreenPreview` render through `ScreenView`; `useMetadataLocale()` derives from `useObjectTranslation().language` (`metadata-admin/i18n.ts:6715`), so under a zh designer the preview's fallback and Studio's own chrome agree.
- **Pins** (`ScreenView.selectPlaceholderLocale-11220.test.tsx`): the zh fallback is the zh pack's `common.select` and not the en word (guarded by `zhWord !== enWord`, so an English literal cannot satisfy it); the en fallback; the provider-less fallback is the en word, not the raw key; CONTROL, an authored placeholder verbatim under zh; an authored `''` stays empty. That is both triage pins plus the `??` pin, asserted on key identity, not copy. Red-first, green and the three ablations are reported on the card; the head's `Test` shards are the CI verdict on the green.
- **`config-field-renderer.tsx:138` left as is — accepted, with the reach stated.** Triage asked "measure whether it is user-facing; if not, say why it stays". The PR says why (measurement 4 and its acceptance notes): the only in-repo producers are plugin-dashboard's four select fields (`refreshIntervalSeconds`, `theme`, `type`, `colorVariant`), each carrying a `defaultValue` (verified at the head), so the trigger draws the option label, never the placeholder; the panels mount only via `DashboardWithConfig`, which nothing in-tree mounts; and it is not an SDUI-registered node. One dimension the PR does not spell out: `ConfigFieldRenderer` is a public export of `@object-ui/components` (`custom/index.ts`, re-exported from the root index), so a downstream host's own `ConfigPanelRenderer` schema with a default-less select is a public door — with zero measured reach in this tree. The PR names the route if a producer appears (the package's existing `createSafeTranslation` table with `common.select`, no new dependency or prop). That satisfies the grade.
- **Public surface:** no export, prop, type or dependency-edge change. `ScreenView` and `ScreenFieldInput` are not root exports of `@object-ui/app-shell` (only `FlowRunner` is); their props are unchanged. The one published-behaviour change is the `''` case, which triage directed.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11220-screen-select-placeholder-i18n.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. Right: two source files of one released package changed; a behaviour fix in a published bundle with no API change; app-shell sits in the repo's single `fixed` group, so the group bumps together at patch (`Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Declaration` all `success`). `Clause-②: no` on the PR body, matching the claim: nothing declared, exported or typed changes; the import of `@object-ui/i18n` is an already-declared dependency; the claim's re-judge condition (a new published prop on `@object-ui/components`) did not arise because `config-field-renderer.tsx` is untouched.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none. Deviations, each answered:
- The diff is wider than the one fallback line (the `t` to `kind` rename): answered in ① — needed so the gate reads the call site; behaviour unchanged.
- Commit trailers and PR footer use the repo's model-free form: a house-rule choice, not a contract matter.
- A throwaway runtime probe was created, run and deleted uncommitted: nothing of it is in the diff (3 files, as listed); fine.
- The views suite ran as one 4-shard lock command: a reporting detail; the head's CI shards are the verdict here.
- Worktree and private ref removed: housekeeping.

Out-of-scope findings (four, each "noted, not filed") — judged:
1. `ScreenView`'s other English defaults (`'Save & Continue'`, `'Cancel'`, the no-data-source line): verified callee defaults at `:279`, `:280`, `:286`; `FlowRunner.tsx:533` passes translated `submitText`/`cancelText`, `ScreenPreview.tsx` hides both buttons and passes `tr('engine.screenPreview.noDataSource', locale)`; all three `FlowRunner` mounts (`FlowRunsPage`, `useConsoleActionRuntime`, `RecordDetailView`) pass `dataSource`; and `ScreenView` is not a root export. No public door, no reach: noted is right; nothing to file. A different family from this card (chrome copy, not the select placeholder).
2. `ConfigFieldRenderer`'s select fallback: a public export with zero in-repo reach (①). Same family as this card (a hard-coded `Select…` placeholder). Not fileable on its own under the named-producer gate; it belongs in the family closing card if the seat opens one.
3. `DatasourceResourcePage.tsx:484` enum select `placeholder="Select…"`: the one with a live public door. Studio's datasource form renders a closed select for every driver `configSchema` property that declares `enum` (`:479`–`:489`), and the schemas come from `GET /api/v1/datasources/drivers`, so the producers are objectstack's drivers, outside this repo — reach is unmeasured, not zero. The route already exists in-package with no `i18n.ts` edit: `engine.form.selectEllipsis` (en `Select…`, zh `请选择…`), read today by `SchemaForm.tsx:2151`/`:2179` and `InspectorComboField.tsx:148`. Same family. Escalated to the seat: one measurement (objectstack's driver configSchemas for `enum`) decides it; a hit names the producer, and the family card (this site named, sites 2 and 4 as same-family members) is the seat's one closing card. Not a blocker for this PR: the claim's file surface excluded it.
4. Console `SettingsField.tsx:455` closed select: the arm is reached only when `spec.valueDomain` is absent (`:434`); the dev measured objectstack's settings manifests at `157baa75f2` (every closed select declares a default; the default-less one declares `valueDomain`). Not re-measured here (objectstack source is outside this review's inputs). Zero measured reach; same family; not fileable alone.

Nothing blocking. The PR is a draft at review time.
